name: Stickler Syndrome Type 2

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic ocular abnormalities including high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration, and risk of retinal detachment
Midfacial hypoplasia, cleft palate or Pierre Robin sequence
Early-onset arthropathy, joint hypermobility, and spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia
Identification of pathogenic variants in COL11A1 gene
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major clinical features (ocular, orofacial, musculoskeletal) with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for COL11A1 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

imaging: Radiographs showing spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia and epiphyseal abnormalities
Ophthalmologic imaging demonstrating vitreoretinal degeneration and retinal detachment
other: Audiometry confirming sensorineural and/or conductive hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: COL2A1 gene mutations instead of COL11A1
More severe ocular manifestations including membranous vitreous anomaly
Similar facial features but with less severe ocular involvement
Different genetic etiology involving COL11A1 mutations with variable expressivity

redFlags: Sudden onset of visual loss indicating retinal detachment
Respiratory distress in neonates due to Pierre Robin sequence
Early-onset severe joint pain and deformities
references: Rose PS, et al. Stickler Syndrome: Clinical Features and Molecular Genetics. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020.
Richards AJ, et al. The Clinical and Molecular Genetics of Stickler Syndrome. J Med Genet. 2019.
